The textContent property of the Node interface represents the text content of the node and its descendants.
textContent and HTMLElement.innerText are easily confused
Setting textContent on a node removes all of the node's children and replaces them with a single text node with the given string value.
Don't get confused by the differences between Node.textContent and HTMLElement.innerText.
We advise against using innerHTML to get or set text inside an element because it deals with raw HTML rather than plain text and can be susceptible to XSS attacks.
